title: Choice overload review
description: The strongest candidates for reducing competing actions and clarifying the primary path.

items.note: Very flat navigation hierarchy; many unrelated destinations compete equally.
Management actions and destructive card actions share one list.
Create link competes with contacts, bank, regional payment, and wallet routes.
Peanut, bank, regional payment, wallet, and support actions are presented together.
The direct-send alternatives compete at the same decision point.
The primary request path competes with several alternative payment rails.
Peanut payment and every alternative rail are presented together.
Add, Send, and Request sit beside activation, card, and verification actions.
Proof of address, identity documents, and support compete without a recommended path.
Sign up, log in, and wallet recovery are all visible at entry.
Continue anyway, notify me, and change country are presented together.
Send, Request, and Join Peanut compete on a guest profile.
Retry, support, and return home are equally available recovery paths.
Home, receipt, and invite actions remain visible after payment.
Receipt, sharing, invitation, download, split, and issue-reporting actions can accumulate.
Two support controls represent the same intent beside the home action.
